messages:
emily: Heads-up — customer tenant `tenant-42` hit a big spike and started getting 502/504s from the hosted API at ~2026-03-17T14:23Z. They reported timeouts and the gateway returned 5xx. Suspect scale-up lag. Request ID: r-9f3b2a.
raj: Can you paste the sample request + headers and the timestamps? Any recent deploys to inference-runtime or autoscaler? Also interested in HPA/KEDA events during that window.
emily: Sample curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "X-Tenant: tenant-42" \
  -d '{"prompt":"short"}'
```
Happened 14:23:12 -> 14:26:00 UTC. No platform deploys in that window according to deploy-bot.
lisa: I pulled k8s events for the tenant's pool:
```
kubectl -n inference get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=inference-tenant-42
... Warning  FailedScaleUp  2026-03-17T14:23:15Z  HorizontalPodAutoscaler  failed to get scale subresource: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
... Normal   ScalingLimited   2026-03-17T14:24:05Z  kube-controller-manager  Scaling limited by resourcequota
```
Also describing ScaledObject shows a long cooldown: `scaledobject.inference.svc/cooldown: 300s` and an annotation I haven't seen before: `autoscaler.redwood.com/scale-suppressed: "true"`.
oncall-bot: ALERT: gateway_5xx_rate for tenant-42 > 8% for 3m (channel: incidents). Pager duty: paged oncall-sre.
raj: That suppression annotation is suspicious. Where did it come from? Could be from a deploy job or a previous operator action.
emily: Customer reported a manual rollback earlier today but not sure if ops toggled anything.
carlos: I checked audit logs for ScaledObject updates: an automated hook from `deploy-runner` added `autoscaler.redwood.com/scale-suppressed=true` during canary cleanup at 14:21:00 to avoid noisy scaleups. It was supposed to be removed after 5m but due to a bug it persisted until 14:40:00.
lisa: That matches the timeline — suppression present during the burst so KEDA ignored external metrics, HPA couldn't compensate because underlying scaled object's behavior constrained scaling. Result: pods stayed low, requests queued -> gateway 502/504s.
raj: Short-term mitigation: remove the annotation, bump minReplicas for that tenant's pool to 3, and trigger warming for model shards. Commands: 
```
kubectl -n inference annotate scaledobject inference-tenant-42 autoscaler.redwood.com/scale-suppressed- || true
kubectl -n inference patch scaledobject inference-tenant-42 -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":3}}' --type=merge
# warm up with low-rate requests to populate KV cache and coldstart models
hey -n 200 -c 20 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx" -H "X-Tenant: tenant-42" -D payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
(hey used for short-probing; adjust to avoid overload)
emily: Did that at 14:45, traffic recovered by 14:52 and customer confirmed lower error rate.
carlos: Root cause: deploy-runner's canary cleanup left suppression annotation when a subsequent retry of cleanup failed. We missed an invariant check. Also cooldown was set to 300s which made recovery slower even after removal.
raj: Action items: 1) patch deploy-runner to remove annotation reliably and add retry/alert when it persists, 2) lower cooldown defaults for ScaledObjects to 90s for bursty tenants or add opt-in prewarm pools, 3) add an alert for "scale-suppressed:true" present >1m for any ScaledObject, 4) add post-incident customer comms and runbook.
lisa: Repro steps for dev/test: create ScaledObject with suppression annotation and run a synthetic burst: 
1) deploy model service with minReplicaCount=1 and scaledobject annotated `autoscaler.redwood.com/scale-suppressed=true`
2) send concurrent traffic `ab -n 100 -c 30` and observe gateway 5xx and HPA not scaling
3) remove annotation and set minReplicaCount->3 and observe recovery times and readiness probe behavior

emily: Customer follow-up: emailed them the timeline, mitigation steps, and ETA for patch. They're OK with the workaround but want guaranteed guardrails.
carlos: I'll own the deploy-runner fix and the alert. Will open PR + changelog and flag for oncall docs.
raj: I'll draft the runbook entry for incidents where scaling suppression correlates with gateway 5xx and add a quick play: "remove suppression -> bump minReplicas -> warm cache." 
emily: Thanks all. Marking incident resolved for now, keeping monitoring on tenant-42 for 24h.
summary: Autoscaler suppression annotation left by deploy-runner + long cooldown caused scale-up lag during burst for tenant-42 -> gateway 5xx/timeouts. Mitigation: remove annotation, bump minReplicas, warm cache. Actions: fix deploy-runner, lower cooldown defaults, alert on suppression.
